title: Understanding the Pattern
text:
The pattern .*:\w+(,\w+)* is designed to match strings that have a colon followed by one or more words separated by commas. Let's break it down:

- .*: matches any character (except for a newline) zero or more times, followed by a colon.
- \w+ matches one or more word characters (letters, digits, or underscores).
- (,\w+)* matches zero or more occurrences of a comma followed by one or more word characters.

title: Analyzing the Match All Cases
text:
Let's analyze the strings in the 'Match all of these below' column:

$$1$$. "total cats petted: 60,102,305"
$$2$$. "my cats' names are: amy,baron,carol"
$$3$$. "the current time is 20:59"

Does the pattern .*:\w+(,\w+)* match all these strings?

title: Analyzing the Match None Cases
text:
Consider the strings that should not be matched:

$$1$$. "total cats petted: sixty, one hundred two, three hundred five"
$$2$$. "my cats' names are: amy, baron, carol"

Does the pattern .*:\w+(,\w+)* avoid matching these strings?

title: Evaluating the Pattern
text: Based on the analysis, does the pattern .*:\w+(,\w+)* fully match all the 'Match all' cases and none of the 'Match none' cases?
